items.headline: US data triple beat at 7:30am CT: claims 189K (vs 197K fcst, prev revised to 195K), Q3 productivity +3.6% (vs 2.8%), ULC -0.7% (vs +0.3%); DXY firmer at 101.47 off the ~101.25 Asia low; 10Y 4.904%
BoE hikes to 4.00% (8-1, Mann for +50bp), first rise since Aug 2023; Bailey: not necessarily the last unless the Middle East conflict is resolved; CPI seen near 5% by mid-2027; GBP/USD steady ~$1.347
Dollar slides to a one-month low (DXY ~101.25, lowest since Sep 30) as the midterm sweep cheers global markets; EUR/USD $1.1261, USD/JPY 157.95, 10Y 4.847% (lowest since Sep 10); Dec Fed hike ~80.7%

RBA's Hauser: 'Inflation is too high, whichever measure you use'; public confidence in the RBA's inflation fight eroding; denies his October remarks were aimed at swaying the board; AUD unmoved ~$0.7013
Oil crash extends in Asia: Brent ~$93.65 (-1.03%), WTI ~$86.98 (-1.29%) as traders keep pricing an end to the Iran conflict after the midterm sweep

Dollar edges lower in Tokyo after the midterm sweep — DXY 101.41 (-0.06% overnight), EUR/USD $1.1241, USD/JPY 158.25, GBP/USD $1.3462 after a 7-week high of $1.3503, AUD/USD $0.7010, NZD/USD $0.5627; BoJ September minutes reinforce December hike bets; BoE decides today
USD/CHF ~0.8140 in Asia, a second straight day lower as the dollar slides after the Democratic sweep; Swiss CPI (1.5% y/y) keeps SNB tightening doubts alive; Dec Fed hike ~82% (CME FedWatch)
Oil settlements confirm the crash: Brent $94.62 (-8.67%) and WTI $88.12 (-8.29%) on Nov 4, Brent lowest since Aug 31, as the Democratic sweep fuels bets on an end to the Iran conflict
Gold spot +3.4% to ~$4,061 on Nov 4 (biggest daily gain since mid-August), silver +5.1% to $52.29; early Asia Nov 5 gold ~$4,139 as the dollar hits a one-month low and yields ease
Rest of today: US claims/productivity/ULC 7:30am CT, Macklem 9:30am, Lagarde 12:00pm, Canada budget 3:00pm CT; payrolls Fri 7:30am CT (FF fcst +65K)

Dollar slides to a one-month low into the NY close — DXY 101.41 (-0.44%), EUR/USD $1.1236 (+0.46%, 4-week high), GBP/USD $1.3475, USD/JPY 158.29, USD/CHF 0.8162 — as Democrats sweep Congress and markets price divided government, tougher AI regulation and less fiscal expansion

Oil crashes ~9%: Brent $94.29 (-9.0%) and WTI $87.70 (-8.7%) from Tuesday's $103.60/$96.09 settles, Brent's lowest since Sep 4, as the White House ties the midterm rout to the Iran war and traders price an end to the conflict; EIA draw (-0.9M) smaller than expected and far below API (-5.3M)
Gold jumps 3.0% past $4,050 — spot $4,059.39, Dec futures settle $4,072.30 — as the dollar hits a one-month low and yields ease (10Y ~4.92%) after the midterm sweep

US data split: ADP BEATS (+86K vs +67K fcst, Sep revised to +86K; services +82K) but ISM services small MISS (54.5 vs 54.8, prices paid 73.0 vs 74.6) — roughly offset into Friday payrolls (fcst +59K, unemployment 4.2%); Dec Fed hike pricing ~83% (CME FedWatch, up from 78.9%)

Eurozone Oct flash CPI inline at 4.0% y/y (prev 3.8%, 3-year high), core steady 2.5% — Dec ECB hike ~89%, no fresh impulse; BoE decides Thu 6:00am CT (hike ~96.7% to 4.00%, vote split and MPR are the event)

Dollar steadies in the Europe morning after the Asia slide: DXY ~101.39, EUR/USD ~1.1251 (+0.6% vs NY close), GBP/USD ~1.3485 (+0.5%), USD/JPY back to ~158.43 from the 157.63 Asia low, USD/CHF ~0.8169; US 10Y ~4.93% — equities turned higher in Europe after the Asia selloff.
items.source: Reuters Europe morning Nov 4 via Devdiscourse — https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/international/4001570-forex-dollar-slips-as-democratic-victories-in-us-midterms-stoke-ai-jitters

items.headline: Eurozone inflation hits a three-year high: flash CPI 4.0% in October (from 3.8%, in line with the Reuters poll), core steady at 2.5%; services 3.3% (from 3.2%), energy 20.8% y/y — firms December ECB hike bets.
Gold reclaims $4,000: XAU/USD ~$4,041 as the midterm sweep sets up divided government; traders price a December Fed hike at ~82% (CME FedWatch).

Oil rebounds in the Europe morning: Brent ~$104.36 (+0.7%), WTI ~$96.72 (+0.7%) at 0730 GMT, reversing early declines, as traders weigh US-Iran war/diplomacy uncertainty after the midterm sweep; EIA official data due 9:30am CT.
FXStreet early Wednesday: NZD/USD gathers momentum above 0.5600 (+~0.4% on the day) after the jobs miss; AUD/USD climbs back toward 0.7000 as equities rebound; USD/CAD ~1.396.
